subject.title: WhatsApp inter_session delivery requests can be wrongly suppressed as REPLY_SKIP / ANNOUNCE_SKIP / NO_REPLY

question: Should OpenClaw fix this WhatsApp inter-session source-reply suppression with the narrow requester-return-path/message-tool guidance in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97311, or defer to the broader structured handoff design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/33478?
rationale: Current source shows a real suppression path, but changing it means choosing model-facing A2A source-reply semantics and coordinating with prompt-cache and reverse-send guard work.

options.title: Review the narrow return-path PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97311 as the current fix candidate after it satisfies the existing message-delivery/security review concerns and keeps the prompt-cache contract intact.

options.title: Defer to structured handoff design
options.body: Keep this issue open under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/33478 until maintainers choose typed delivery-intent or structured callback semantics.

options.title: Require fresh WhatsApp proof first
options.body: Keep the issue blocked on a current-main redacted WhatsApp transcript before changing A2A prompt behavior.

recommendation.title: Review the narrow return-path PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97311 as the current fix candidate after it satisfies the existing message-delivery/security review concerns and keeps the prompt-cache contract intact.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent sessions_send routing and delivery history plus merger of the prompt-cache PR make this the best available owner for the narrow source-reply contract choice.
